newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares fall as U.S. rate fears intensify.
newsitem.headline: German shares fall as U.S. rate fears intensify.

text.p: German shares closed sharply lower on Monday amid profit-taking after recent rallies and continuing uncertainty ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve meeting on Tuesday.
The 30-share DAX index ended bourse trade down 19.06 points at 2,627.04, or a loss of 0.72 percent for the session. In late electronic trade, the IBIS DAX index closed further down at 2,624.18.

Dealers said the DAX was under pressure ahead of the U.S. central bank meeting and speculation of a U.S. rate increase. Some traders said the market at current levels had now factored in a small increase in U.S. rates.
"People are holding off ahead of the Fed and are generally unwilling to buy at these levels," said one trader, referring to the record highs reached by German shares in recent days.
Dollar-sensitive chemical shares were unable to buck the downward trend despite a firm dollar, with Hoechst AG falling 34 pfennigs to 54.91 marks and BASF down 60 pfennigs at 47.18 marks.
Insurance group Munich Re traded fairly well on its DAX 30 debut, ending eight marks higher at 3,458 marks in cash trade but slipping sveen marks to 3,456 on IBIS.
Linotype-Hell AG ended up seven marks at 130 marks after Linotype chief executive said he would quit. He will be replaced by an executive from Linotype's new owner, Heidelberger Druck.
